summary: Djibouti's immigration directorate issues eVisas through its official portal, evisa.gouv.dj: a short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and a standard one up to 90. The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry; the UK Foreign Office says a tourist visa can still be bought on arrival, paid in cash in US dollars.

notes: The UK Foreign Office says photographing infrastructure such as ports, public buildings, airports, military facilities and bridges is prohibited; your equipment could be confiscated and you could be arrested.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says credit and debit cards are not widely accepted, and where they are you often need a Visa card. ATMs are normally available in Djibouti City but may not accept Mastercard, so carry enough cash.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel to the Djibouti–Eritrea border, where there are unmarked landmines. It says there is a risk of petty crime and advises keeping valuables, particularly cameras and passports, out of sight, staying on paved roads and avoiding travel outside city centres after dark.

tips.text: The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry, and that once approved it is downloaded as a PDF. The UK Foreign Office says a tourist visa can also be bought on arrival, paid in cash in US dollars.
The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to the Djibouti–Eritrea border, and Canada advises against non-essential travel within 10 km of it. There are unmarked landmines near the border.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Djibouti?
faq.answer: Yes. Djibouti issues eVisas before travel through the official portal evisa.gouv.dj. A short-stay eVisa covers up to 14 days and a standard one up to 90 days.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Djibouti?
faq.answer: The official sources differ. The eVisa portal says the eVisa replaces the visa issued at the point of entry, usually an airport or border crossing; the UK Foreign Office says you can buy a tourist visa when you arrive, paid in cash in US dollars, or apply online before travelling.

faq.question: How much does the Djibouti eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The official eVisa portal lists USD 12 for a visa of up to 14 days and USD 23 for a stay of 15 to 90 days, plus 10% VAT added at payment.
